# faraday_stream (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "faraday_stream" "orders" {
  name = "orders"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `category` (String) A broad category describing the flavor of a stream property.
- `deprecated` (Boolean) Whether the stream is deprecated.
- `deprecation_notes` (String) Notes about the deprecation of the stream.
- `description` (String) A description of the stream.
- `literate` (String) A human-readable name for the stream.
- `name` (String)
- `properties` (Attributes Map) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--properties))
- `tier` (String) A billing tier for a stream property.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) If not null, this resource will no longer receive updates, but will still be visable.
- `created_at` (String) When this resource was created.
- `event_contribution_by_dataset` (Attributes List) Details of events emitted by each dataset into the stream. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--event_contribution_by_dataset))
- `event_count` (Number) Number of events in the stream.
- `id` (String) A unique ID for this resource.
- `last_read_input_at` (String) The last time this resource's input was read.
- `last_updated_config_at` (String) The last time this resource's configuration was updated. If this is more recent than last_updated_output_at, the resource will be rebuilt.
- `last_updated_output_at` (String) The last time this resource successfully built.
- `newest_date` (String) Date of the most recent event in the stream.
- `oldest_date` (String) Date of the first event in the stream.
- `resource_type` (String) The type of this resource.
- `status` (String) The current state of this resource and any updates.
- `status_changed_at` (String) When the status of this resource was last updated.
- `status_error` (String) If this resource has `status == "error"`, this will contain an error message.
- `updated_at` (String) When this resource was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--properties"></a>
### Nested Schema for `properties`

Optional:

- `directionality_interpretation` (String) If applicable, describe the meaning of any directionality in the values.
- `interpretation_map` (String) For enumerable values, a mapping from value to its interpretation. Key type matches the property type, value is always a string. Free-form; supply JSON via jsonencode().
- `null_value_interpretation` (String) If a unary null replacement is not applicable or viable, describe how NULLs should be interpreted when encountered.
- `statistical_type` (String) A string describing the nature of data represented by the trait. categorical_nominal: the field contains one value of an unordered bounded set. Example: "preferred_channel" — one of "email", "sms", "direct_mail". categorical_ordinal: the field contains one value of an ordered bounded set. Example: "spending_tier" — one of "low", "medium", "high", "premium". multicategorical_nominal: the field contains one or more values of an unordered bounded set. Example: "interests" — "outdoors", "travel", "fitness". continuous_ordinal: the field contains numeric values with a natural ordering. Example: "lifetime_value". binary: the field contains boolean-like values representing presence/absence. Example: "has_pool" — true or false. count: the field contains non-negative integer counts. Example: "children_count" — 0, 1, 2, 3. interval: the field contains numeric values where differences are meaningful but ratios are not. Example: "date_of_birth" as epoch. ratio: the field contains numeric values where both differences and ratios are meaningful, with a true zero. Example: "age" — 0, 25, 50. Type compatibility (new values only): - continuous_ordinal requires a numeric type (long, float, double). - categorical_nominal requires string or boolean. - categorical_ordinal requires string. - multicategorical_nominal requires array_of_strings. Deprecated values (still accepted, will be removed in a future version): categorical: equivalent to categorical_nominal. multicategorical: equivalent to multicategorical_nominal. ordinal: ambiguous — prefer categorical_ordinal or continuous_ordinal. nominal: ambiguous — prefer categorical_nominal.
- `type` (String) The data type of a column in table, or of a trait. Types are expressed using a subset of [Avro](https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html). Possible values include: - boolean: A Boolean value. - long: A 64-bit integer. - double: A 64-bit float. - string: A Unicode string, possibly representing categorical data. - date: A date with no reference to time of day.
- `unit` (String) For numeric types, in what units is the data stored.

Read-Only:

- `breaks` (List of Number) For continuous data types, list of reasonable cutoff values.
- `categories` (List of String) For STRING type, list of allowed values.
- `distribution` (Attributes List) Counts corresponding to the existing breaks property. Only available when the property is numerical, otherwise empty. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--properties--distribution))
- `emitted_by_datasets` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--properties--emitted_by_datasets))
- `values` (Attributes List) Top 100 observed values of this property. Only available when the property is categorical or multicategorical, otherwise empty. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--properties--values))

<a id="nestedatt--event_contribution_by_dataset"></a>
### Nested Schema for `event_contribution_by_dataset`

Read-Only:

- `dataset_id` (String) The dataset the column comes from
- `event_count` (Number)
- `newest_date` (String) The most recent event this dataset contributed. Omitted when it contributed no events, and when the stream has no dated data.
- `oldest_date` (String) The first event this dataset contributed. Omitted when it contributed no events, and when the stream has no dated data.
- `parsing` (Attributes List) How well this dataset's declared formats were read, one entry per column that declares one. Omitted when no column in this dataset declares a format for the stream, and for contributions measured before this was reported. Neither case means every value was read successfully. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--event_contribution_by_dataset--parsing))

<a id="nestedatt--event_contribution_by_dataset--parsing"></a>
### Nested Schema for `event_contribution_by_dataset.parsing`

Read-Only:

- `candidate_row_count` (Number) Rows of the dataset available to this stream.
- `column_name` (String) The dataset column the values are read from.
- `examples` (List of String) A sample of the values that could not be read, to compare against the declared format.
- `format` (String) The format declared for this column, which says how its values should be read.
- `parsed_row_count` (Number) Populated rows whose value could be read as the declared format. Divided by `populated_row_count` this is the read rate, which should be 100%; any shortfall means the values and the declared format disagree.
- `populated_row_count` (Number) Candidate rows where the column held a value. An empty column is not a failure to read one.
- `stale_before` (String) The date those rows were judged against: anything earlier was treated as implausible. The bound is relative to when the stream was built, so it is reported rather than left to be recalculated against a different day. Present only when rows were actually excluded.
- `stale_examples` (List of String) A sample of the values that were read successfully but resolved to an implausible date. These never appear in `examples`, because nothing went wrong when reading them — seeing them is the only way to tell that, say, `01/02/03` read as `mm_dd_yyyy_slash` became the year 3.
- `stale_row_count` (Number) Rows whose value was read successfully but produced a date too far in the past to be plausible, which usually means the format is being misread rather than that the data is old. These rows are excluded from the stream.
- `stream_property` (String) The stream property these values populate.
